subject: Acme - traffic heatmap requests and calibration
content:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme-health.com>, Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acme-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - traffic heatmap requests and calibration

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can size and validate a target SLO in our proposal:

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary endpoints: /api/v1/assist and /stream/chat (the latter is streaming, server-sent events).
- Traffic pattern: short user bursts (10–30s) during business hours, with evening spike for telehealth windows.
- Current SLAs: P95 latency target ~150ms for non-streaming; P99 target ~350ms.
- Tokenization: payloads are mixed (short prompts + occasional long history). You mentioned average character length but not tokenized counts.

Concrete information we need to proceed with accurate throughput sizing:
1) A 72‑hour telemetry extract (CSV) with per-request rows including: timestamp (ISO), endpoint, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, user_id (hashed), and whether the session used streaming. If you can include tokenized_input_length and tokenized_output_length that is ideal.
2) Clarify peak window assumptions: are your spikes concentrated in <2 minute windows, or are they spread across 5–15 minute windows?
3) Concurrent open streaming connections at peak (approx): how many simultaneous open streams do you expect for /stream/chat?
4) Target latency preferences mapped to endpoints (we heard global 150/350 numbers; confirm if streaming has a different tail bound).

What we'll do once we receive the sample:
- Run a quick heatmap analysis (tokens/sec by endpoint and 1/5/15 minute QPS windows).
- Produce a proposed dedicated capacity profile showing steady-state vs. peak requirements and suggested autoscale thresholds.
- Highlight batching and KV-cache opportunities to reduce per-token cost for repeated histories.

Attachments: example CSV schema is attached as acme-telemetry-sample.csv (empty header row in this email). Also attaching a short-sizing sketch (redwood-sizing-proposal-v1.pdf) with initial mapping of tokens->costs.

Proposed next step: a 30-minute calibration call tomorrow to walk the exported sample with us and confirm mapping assumptions. I'm available 10:00–12:00 PT. If that works, we'll also request temporary permission to ingest the sample into a sandbox project so we can generate the heatmap quickly (read-only ingestion; no customer-identifying info will be stored).

Thanks — we want to make sure our proposal matches your operational reality rather than hypothetical peaks.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

---
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme-health.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acme-health.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - traffic heatmap requests and calibration

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a redacted 72‑hour sample (acme-telemetry-sample.csv). It includes: timestamp, endpoint, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, is_streaming, tokenized_input_length (approx), tokenized_output_length (approx). All user_ids are hashed.

Answers inline:
- Peak windows: we see very short sharp spikes (~30–90s) during certain clinician shift handoffs, plus a more sustained evening surge (5–20 minutes) for telehealth check-ins.
- Concurrent open streams at peak: roughly 180–220 simultaneous streams during the highest telehealth evenings. These originate across three primary regions (mostly us-west).
- Latency targets: Non-streaming endpoints: P95 < 150ms, P99 < 325–350ms. Streaming: start-of-response latency should be < 250ms for first token; tail delivery is less strict but should avoid multi-second stalls.

We are ok with Redwood ingesting the sample into a temporary sandbox for calibration. Procurement will circulate an NDA addendum; procurement contact is procurement@acme-health.com.

Attaching CSV: acme-telemetry-sample.csv

—Alice
Alice Tan
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
alice.tan@acme-health.com | +1 (650) 555-3344

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme-health.com>, Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acme-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - traffic heatmap requests and calibration

Thanks Alice — this is great and very actionable. A couple follow-ups / clarifications before we run the heatmap: 

1) Token mapping: you noted tokenized lengths are approximate. Can you confirm the tokenizer you used (GPT‑style BPE, or a custom tokenizer)? If approximate, please include the character->token estimation rule you used (e.g., 4 chars ~= 1 token). That will help us calculate tokens/sec reliably.

2) Region mapping: you mentioned us-west predominately. Can you add a region column if possible (us-west/us-east/eu) for the 72‑hour extract? If not, tell us the top 3 prefixes/IP blocks and we can map.

3) Peak sampling: for the very short spikes (30–90s), do you have server logs with per-second counts for a representative day? If yes, a 1‑minute aggregated and a 10‑second sampled file would really help illustrate the peak profile.

Proposed technical next steps / timeline: 
- Today: we ingest the CSV into a sandbox project (with your permission) and run an automated heatmap that returns tokens/sec per endpoint and 1/5/15 minute QPS windows.
- Tomorrow EOD: we deliver a draft capacity profile (steady vs peak) and an annotated latency/throughput tradeoff table with suggested autoscale thresholds and a fallback routing policy for overflow.

I attached the initial sizing sketch (redwood-sizing-proposal-v1.pdf) that maps your supplied token estimates to a few candidate instance types and a baseline autoscale policy. Please review and let us know any hard constraints (max monthly budget, required reserved capacity, etc.) so we can prioritize cost vs headroom.

For the calibration call, can you do tomorrow at 10:30 AM PT? If that doesn't work, we can do 11:30 AM PT. I'll send a quick calendar invite after you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acme-health.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme-health.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - traffic heatmap requests and calibration

Jonas / team —

Sounds good. NDA addendum is on my side; procurement will loop you in if any more redaction is needed. 10:30 AM PT tomorrow works for Alice and me — calendar invite sent. You have permission to ingest the attached sample into the Redwood sandbox for analysis.

Thanks — see you tomorrow.

-Bob
Bob Jenkins
Director of Engineering, Acme Health
bob.jenkins@acme-health.com | +1 (415) 555-2201
